pharm: Oral third-generation cephalosporin with beta-lactamase stability, active against many Gram-negative respiratory pathogens; bactericidal via inhibition of bacterial cell wall synthesis.
quick: 400 mg orally once daily for 10 days
Take suspension on empty stomach (2 h before or 1 h after food)
Category B; use only if clearly needed
Renal function; signs of C. difficile colitis
summary: Ceftibuten (Cedax) is an oral third-generation cephalosporin for mild-to-moderate infections: acute bacterial exacerbations of chronic bronchitis, acute bacterial otitis media, and pharyngitis/tonsillitis caused by susceptible organisms. Adults take 400 mg once daily for 10 days; pediatric dose is 9 mg/kg once daily (max 400 mg). Dose is reduced in renal impairment. Cross-reactivity with penicillin allergy and C. difficile colitis are key warnings.
indications: Acute bacterial exacerbations of chronic bronchitis due to H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis, or S. pneumoniae
Acute bacterial otitis media due to H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis, or S. pyogenes
Pharyngitis and tonsillitis due to S. pyogenes

dosage.n: Maximum 400 mg/day; use weight-based suspension chart

dosage.t: At the end of each hemodialysis session

admin: Capsules may be taken without regard to food
Administer the oral suspension on an empty stomach: at least 2 hours before or 1 hour after a meal
Reconstituted suspension is stable 14 days refrigerated (2-8 C)
Complete the full 10-day course even if symptoms improve
Reduce dose in moderate-to-severe renal impairment
moa: Bactericidal action by binding to essential penicillin-binding proteins and inhibiting synthesis of the bacterial cell wall; as a third-generation cephalosporin it is highly stable to many beta-lactamases.

absolute: Known allergy to the cephalosporin class of antibiotics
relative: History of penicillin or other beta-lactam allergy (up to ~10% cross-reactivity)

preg: Pregnancy Category B; not teratogenic in animals at high doses. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether ceftibuten is excreted in human milk at recommended dosages; exercise caution when administering to a nursing mother.
renal: Dose reduction required for CrCl <50 mL/min: 200 mg q24h for CrCl 30-49 mL/min and 100 mg q24h for CrCl 5-29 mL/min. Hemodialysis removes ceftibuten; give a single 400 mg dose at the end of each session. Seizures possible if dose not reduced.

minor: Antacids (single dose did not affect absorption)
interactions.food: Take suspension on an empty stomach (2 h before or 1 h after food); capsules may be taken with or without food
interactions.diagnostics: May cause a false-positive direct Coombs test.

serious: Seizures (in renal impairment without dose reduction)

monitoring: Renal function, especially in the elderly and dialysis patients
Signs of C. difficile-associated diarrhea during and after therapy
Signs of superinfection or resistant organisms
Hypersensitivity reactions, particularly in penicillin-allergic patients
counsel: Take the oral suspension 2 hours before or 1 hour after meals
Complete the full prescribed 10-day course even if you feel better
Stop and seek care for severe or bloody diarrhea, which can occur during or weeks after treatment
Tell your doctor about any penicillin or cephalosporin allergy
The suspension contains sucrose (about 1 g per teaspoon) - relevant if you have diabetes
pk: Capsules 2-25 C; reconstituted suspension 2-8 C, use within 14 days
pearls: One of the few oral third-generation cephalosporins; convenient once-daily dosing for respiratory infections
Highly stable to many common beta-lactamases
Weak/inconsistent activity against S. pneumoniae and S. aureus - not ideal for serious pneumococcal disease
Readily dialyzable (~65% removed by a single hemodialysis session)
Reduce dose for CrCl <50 mL/min to avoid CNS toxicity/seizures
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume the regular schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: No specific antidote; may cause cerebral irritation leading to convulsions. Manage supportively; hemodialysis effectively removes ceftibuten (~65% of plasma concentration in a single session).
